statements.quote: it is structured to benefit Wall Street, the wealthy and the rich
statements.claim: Criticizes the structure of PPP relief as favoring large financial interests over small businesses. This is not a statement opposing every pandemic relief package.

statements.quote: I would have voted for that bill
statements.claim: Says she would have supported the relief bill under discussion and would work with Speaker Pelosi on another stimulus package.

statements.quote: The reduction of our NYPD budget
statements.claim: Supports reducing the NYPD budget and links that spending to forgone investments in education and public housing. No opponent's policing stance is inferred from reporter summaries.
Calls for universal basic income in the pandemic context. This quotation is not compared to an invented AOC rejection of the proposal.

statements.quote: I will never walk away from this community.
statements.claim: Responds to criticism about her focus by affirming commitment to the community; this is a campaign statement, not a measured constituent-service outcome.

comparisons.analysis: Ocasio-Cortez emphasizes opposition to corporate-favoring relief design; Caruso-Cabrera emphasizes passing the package and pursuing further aid. The reports use overlapping PPP/CARES/relief-bill references, so this records stated legislative strategies rather than inventing a precisely identified common vote or a blanket pro-/anti-relief distinction.

Dolan says the Gaza war is not central to district concerns; Ocasio-Cortez explicitly argues that international policy translates into local resource decisions. These are different campaign frames, not independent findings about what all constituents prioritize.
